key_lookups.note: THREE roles + ONE equivalent duplicate (NOT four roles). The twins share cmp fn 0x52B720-family and rehash/sort worker 0x7C8B48 (qsort-shaped), but sharing a skeleton does NOT imply equal semantics for 0x52B390 / 0x52B430. R-055 first draft wrongly called 0x52B430 a second bool lookup -- it mistook the first ret of the SEPARATE function 0x52B4D0 for 0x52B430 tail. R-056 first draft made three further errors caught by cross-family blind verify: (a) function length 0x77 -> 0x79 (ret imm16 is THREE bytes; the 0x77 window cut the trailing 00 and made a 7-byte nop fence look like 10); (b) called 0x52B620 dead weight -- it has 20 callers; (c) attributed +0x2C to this+0x2C, but 0x528A10 does `add esi,0x2c` from [ebp+8] at 0x528A86, so it is [ebp+8]+0x2C, a DIFFERENT object. See G-77.

key_lookups.0x52B620: ALIAS of 0x52B4F0 -- byte-for-byte duplicate (0x79 = 121 bytes each, exactly 4 differing bytes, ALL operands: cmp-fn imm32 0x52B6A0 vs 0x52B720, and the low 2 bytes of the rel32 of the same `call 0x7C8B48`; the two cmp fns are byte-identical, 34 bytes). The twins' inlined 10-byte loop core (8bc1992bc2d1f88b34c7) is byte-identical between them but DIFFERS from the kernel 0x52B6D0's own copy (8bc6992bc2d1f88b3cc1: different register allocation). NOT dead weight: it has 20 callers of its own (aligned linear sweep found 68,249 call sites in .text).
